How to scope an MVP without building too much

A step-by-step method to scope a minimum viable product: one core action, one user, and a written list of what you won't build.

DigitalBurj Editorial

7 min read · 22 July 2026

On this page

  1. 1. Name the user and the problem
  2. 2. Choose the core action
  3. 3. Write the 'won't build' list
  4. 4. Decide the success signal

Key takeaways

  • ✓ Define the one core action first.
  • ✓ Write down what you won't build.
  • ✓ Measure behaviour, not compliments.

1. Name the user and the problem

Pick one type of user and describe the problem in their words. If you can't find ten people who have it, stop here.

2. Choose the core action

What is the single action that delivers value? Booking a slot, submitting a document, getting a quote. Everything in the MVP exists to make that action work.

3. Write the 'won't build' list

List every feature you are deliberately leaving out: admin dashboards, integrations, settings, notifications. This list protects the budget more than any estimate.

4. Decide the success signal

Before building, agree what result means continue, change or stop — for example, 30% of sign-ups completing the core action in their first week.
